title: Built a tool to help with generating 2D game assets - looking for feedback
author: Chologism
selftext:
Hey everyone. I'm an experienced Unity dev and I've always struggled with getting quick assets for my projects and jams. To help with that, I built Spritecook.ai.

It's meant for generating 2D assets and pixel art fast so you can stay focused on the code. It is still in the early stages, but I am looking for some feedback from other devs on how it fits into your workflow.

You can try it out here: [https://spritecook.ai](https://spritecook.ai)

Let me know what you think.

https://preview.redd.it/1qtji2okmdbg1.png?width=2560&format=png&auto=webp&s=ebdc6489d5560a8e6a23ca141e6ff26c485c69c4

replies.author: Chologism

comments.author: EmotionalFan5429
comments.body: Dude, you're 2+ years late for the party. Simple 2D images are easy to generate.

replies.author: Chologism
replies.body: fair point. I originally built this as a cli tool for myself just to stop repeating the same style/theme descriptions in every prompt. i only put it online recently because I found it super useful, and the models finally got good enough to stay consistent across a whole project.

comments.author: Awesome_Teo
comments.body:
It's actually convenient so you don't have to enter prompts/set up the style every time. Well, I'll say this: it's a cool tool, but I wouldn't be willing to pay extra for it. Or even, I'd buy an app like this so I could install it locally and use it with local models or my own API keys. Otherwise, the project only survives as long as you pay for hosting, and as often happens with such small web apps, they simply disappear one day.

https://preview.redd.it/m8u7290gsebg1.png?width=1024&format=png&auto=webp&s=f4fd118b279c0d553bd90abbde5aa531b27d03f5

replies.author: Chologism
replies.body: Being able to use your own API keys is an interesting one, noted!

comments.author: florvas
comments.body:
Late to the party, but do you ever do discounts? I know the service is already reasonably cheap at the base tier, but I'm relatively inexperienced giving AI good prompts - based on my experience trying it out, the base tier would likely be enough credits to make and animate a single character (in what will eventually be an RPG, no less). Much as I'd love to hire someone with artistic talent or just pay for the service, this is pretty much being made all at my expense, in my spare time, while I work two jobs to keep the family afloat while my wife looks for work. 

Advice to that end would be welcome too, if that's not too much trouble. I've got plenty of experience as a software engineer, but until this past year I've been avoiding using AI as much as possible, and have zero natural artistic talent. Struggling to find a middle ground between actually hiring artists, and just flipping free assets.
